exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, forceps delivery, elective Cesarean section, emergency Cesarean section)
outcome: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) on POP-Q staging: uterine prolapse, cystocele, rectocele
Ballooning of the levator ani muscle (LAM) hiatus
cohort: 202 primiparous women who delivered at a tertiary hospital with 9000 deliveries per annum
finding: Clinically significant POP was common postpartum, and levator avulsion, significantly associated with forceps delivery, was seen in 29% of participants and was associated with POP and related symptoms.
mod_finding: Forceps delivery was associated with an increased risk of levator ani muscle abnormality (OR 4.9, 95% CI 1.44-16.97) and postnatal POP symptoms were negatively associated with both elective (OR 0.2, 95% CI 0.09-0.63) and emergency (OR 0.3, 95% CI 0.12-0.83) Cesarean section.
